name: block_counting_ui_integration
description: Master instructions for GitHub Copilot to integrate block counting question JSON files into the AFOQT study app with a reusable isometric block renderer and CSS.

grid.description: Logical layout of stack positions on the floor.

fields.cols: number of columns, from left (0) to right (cols-1)
fields.rows: number of rows, from front (0) to back (rows-1)

fields.height: integer count of cubes in this stack, 0 means empty cell

rules: All stacks must have 0 <= col < grid.cols and 0 <= row < grid.rows.
height must be a non negative integer.
Each (row,col) pair should appear at most once.

renderingNotes: Use CSS generated isometric tiles to draw each cube layer.
Sort cubes by row, then height, then column to keep overlap drawing order correct.
Use a fixed logical cube size (for example 32px) and scale to fit uiSpec.width and uiSpec.height.
Use three visible faces per cube (top, left, right) with simple shading to suggest depth.
Empty stacks (height 0) show only floor tile or nothing based on design choice.

layout: Use position: relative on the scene container.
Place each cube with position: absolute and transform translate to pseudo isometric coordinates.
Use a consistent z-index scheme so back rows and higher layers render behind front lower layers.
Keep colors neutral but distinct between faces so the student can easily separate stacks.
accessibility: Ensure the contrast between cubes and background is high enough to read heights.
Allow a high contrast theme by using CSS variables for cube colors.

responsibilities: Convert each stack into per layer cube positions.
Render an isometric projection as a purely visual component.
Do not handle question text or answer logic.

props.question: single question object from block_counting JSON

responsibilities: Render multiple choice answers A through D as buttons or selectable options.
Optionally highlight the correct answer when in review mode.

BlockCountingPreview.purpose: Dev preview screen for manual QA of all block_counting questions.
dataFlow: Allow the developer to step through questions sequentially.
Render BlockCountingQuestion for the current question.

dataLoading.approach: Use the same loader utilities used by table reading and instrument comprehension.
contract: Each JSON file exports a top level object that matches jsonContract.questionFileShape.
The app maps over questions array to generate screens.
subjectId and difficulty are used for navigation and filtering.

generatorRules.style: Match AFOQT and Trivium style block counting logic.

beginner: Simple totals, row or column sums, above ground counts, stacks with exact heights.
advanced: Include transformations such as add one cube to each stack, remove whole rows or columns, compare totals across rows and columns.
expert: Multi step reasoning such as before and after figures, counts by condition, and combined constraints.
More trap distractors that match partial reasoning.

c1Tutoring.requirement: Every question must include explanation, steps, and fastStrategy fields that follow the C1 method.
stepsPattern: Step 1 identify what the question is really asking (total blocks, above ground blocks, ground contact, specific height stacks, etc).
Step 2 identify the main rule or pattern (sum of heights, height minus one, row or column focus, before minus after).
Step 3 break the solution into micro additions and subtractions, usually row by row or column by column.
Step 4 reinforce why the correct count matches the figure and why it fits the requested condition.
Step 5 describe at least one common error such as double counting a stack, ignoring empty stacks, or forgetting the ground contact rule.

fastStrategyRules: Use row sums or column sums instead of counting cubes visually.
For blocks not touching the ground, convert each height h into h minus 1 and sum those.
For ground touching blocks, count non empty stacks.
For uniform rows or columns, multiply height by stack count instead of repeated addition.
When a whole row or column is removed or added, adjust the total by that row or column total instead of recomputing everything.

copilotTasks: Create the BlockStackIso React component that renders uiSpec.type === 'block_stack_iso' using the CSS contract defined here.
Create BlockCountingQuestion and BlockCountingPreview components that read block_counting JSON files and render interactive questions.
Wire block counting into the main subject selection and navigation system using subjectId === 'block_counting'.
Add unit tests that validate correct total block counts based on uiSpec.stacks for a small sample of questions.
Ensure the renderer can handle all beginner uiSpec layouts used in block_counting_beginner_part1.json and block_counting_beginner_part2.json.
testingChecklist: Visually confirm that each stack height in the renderer matches the JSON uiSpec for a random sample of questions.
Verify that total block counts from automated helpers match the answer field for sample questions.
Check that empty stacks (height 0) do not render cubes.
Confirm that performance remains acceptable with the largest beginner grid size and maximum heights.
Confirm that the same BlockStackIso component can be reused unchanged for advanced and expert JSON files as they are added.
